events.title: Washington's Army Settles into Valley Forge
events.description: The Continental Army, led by George Washington, marched into winter quarters at Valley Forge, Pennsylvania. Over the following months, the troops endured harsh cold, shortages and disease.
events.significance: Valley Forge became a symbol of American perseverance. The army trained there under Baron von Steuben and emerged as a more disciplined fighting force.

events.title: A Christmas Carol Is Published
events.description: Charles Dickens's novella about the miser Ebenezer Scrooge and his change of heart after visits from three spirits went on sale in London.
events.significance: The story helped shape the modern idea of Christmas, with its themes of generosity and goodwill. It has never gone out of print and has been adapted countless times.

events.title: The BBC Launches Its Empire Service
events.description: The BBC began shortwave broadcasts to listeners across the British Empire, under the name BBC Empire Service.
events.significance: The service later became the BBC World Service. It is now one of the largest international broadcasters in the world.

events.title: The First Indochina War Begins
events.description: Viet Minh forces attacked French military positions and homes in Hanoi, which started open war between France and the Viet Minh.
events.significance: The conflict lasted until 1954 and ended French colonial rule in Indochina. It set the stage for later conflict in Vietnam.

events.title: Andrei Sakharov Released from Internal Exile
events.description: Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev freed the physicist and dissident Andrei Sakharov after six years of internal exile in the city of Gorky.
events.significance: The release was an early sign of glasnost, the Soviet policy of greater openness. It marked a shift in how the USSR treated dissent.
